update.title: Built a local AI scene-tracking pipeline
update.summary: Built an agent pipeline that turns narrative messages into typed scene state through focused worker loops and constrained tool calls.

preview.description: Illustrated tavern scene beside structured scene-state JSON

blocks.body:
## Turn narrative input into structured state

Scene Tracker processes each message as a state-building task. It combines the message with the current chat state, runs the configured agents, and returns an updated scene.

Useful details become typed characters, objects, locations, and scene context that the next message can reuse.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  Input[Message + current state] --> Context[Build step context]
  Context --> Loop[Focused agent loop]
  Loop -->|Tool call| Tool[Apply structured state change]
  Tool --> Loop
  Loop -->|Step complete| Scheduler[Release dependent steps]
  Scheduler -->|More work| Context
  Scheduler -->|Pipeline complete| Result[Updated state + processing trace]
blocks.description: A message moves through focused agent loops, constrained state tools, dependency scheduling, and an explicit result. Each agent loops through reasoning and tool calls until its step is complete, then releases any work that depends on it.

blocks.body:
## Give each agent a focused role

Agents specialize in characters, clothing, emotions, objects, scene details, or relevance. Independent steps can run together, while dependent steps wait for the state they need.

Each role receives only the context and tools configured for its job, keeping the pipeline modular instead of relying on one all-purpose prompt.

## Use tool calls as the state boundary

Agents turn their findings into constrained calls that create entities, update attributes, move objects, or record scene changes. Those calls produce typed state instead of leaving the result buried in model prose.

blocks.description: A shortened retained run result shows the response boundary: step outcomes, applied mutations, timing, and the updated state.

blocks.body:
## Keep each run inspectable

The response records which steps ran, whether they succeeded, how many tool calls they made, and which changes were applied.

The same lifecycle is logged across worker starts, completions, and errors, making a slow or incorrect extraction step easier to trace.
